paragraphs.text: He stirs up himself and all his affections to praise God.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: That God may have the whole praise: in which he forbids all vain confidence showing that by nature we are more inclined to put our trust in creatures, than in God the Creator.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: As their vain opinions, by which they flattered themselves and so imagined wicked enterprises.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: He encourages the godly to trust only in the Lord, both in his power's ability to deliver them from all danger, and for his promise sake, as his will is most ready to do it.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Whose faith and patience for a while he tries but at length he punishes the adversaries, that he may be known to be the judge of the world.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Though he visits them with affliction, hunger, imprisonment and such like, yet his fatherly love and pity never fails them, yea rather to his these are signs of his love.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Meaning, all who are destitute of worldly means and help.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: He assures the Church that God reigns forever for the preservation of the same.
paragraphs.label: h
